Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

extend verb

make longer or larger

also prolong, lengthen, extend a stay, extend a deadline, enlarge, drag out, drag on

classical

Cic. Sen. 46: ad multam noctem … variō sermōne prōdūcimus
Traupman 306
Traupman 339

prōdūcō, prōdūcere, prōdūxī, prōductum

verb, third conjugation

lengthen, prolong (in time or space)

Other words

  • prōrogō, prōrogāre, prōrogāvī, prōrogātum — extend, prolong (a term, a time)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 2.24: nē quīnquennī imperium Caesarī prōrogārētur (Lewis & Short)

  • prōferō, prōferre, prōtulī, prōlātum — extend, enlarge (bounds); put off (a date)

    verb, conjugation · also used · classical · Caes. BC 1.81 (Lewis & Short); Cic. Att. 13.14.1: auctiōnis diem laxius prōferre (Lewis & Short)

  • trahō, trahere, trāxī, tractum — drag out (a war, a business); in the passive, drag on

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 10.8.2: sīn trahitur bellum (Lewis & Short s.v. trahō); Traupman 306

Examples

  • convīviumque vīcīnōrum cotīdiē compleō, quod ad multam noctem quam maximē possumus variō sermōne prōdūcimus

    every day I fill my table with neighbours, and we stretch the party as late into the night as we can with all kinds of talkCic. Sen. 46

See also extend, extension, long.
